Classic Homemade Lemonade

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 6Prep 10 min

Lemonade is a refreshing and iconic beverage often served during Independence Day celebrations in the United States. Its bright, tangy flavor perfectly complements summer barbecues, picnics, and fireworks gatherings, making it a staple for patriotic festivities.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) freshly squeezed lemon juice (about 4-6 lemons)
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 5 cups (1.2 liters) cold water
  • Ice cubes
  • Lemon slices and fresh mint for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. In a small saucepan, combine 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water.
  2. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves completely to make a simple syrup.
  3. Remove from heat and let the syrup cool to room temperature.
  4. In a large pitcher, combine the freshly squeezed lemon juice and the cooled simple syrup.
  5. Add the remaining 4 cups cold water and stir well to mix.
  6. Taste and adjust sweetness or tartness by adding more water or lemon juice if desired.
  7. Refrigerate the lemonade until chilled.
  8. Serve over ice cubes and garnish with lemon slices and fresh mint if desired.

Tips

  • For a sparkling version, replace some or all of the cold water with sparkling water just before serving.
  • Use organic lemons to avoid any pesticide residues, especially if you use the lemon slices as garnish.
  • Add a few crushed fresh raspberries or strawberries for a colorful twist.
